messages:
maria: Quick ask — can someone run a targeted perf + quality sweep for model-x across int4/int8/FP8? Nightly showed a ~12ms P95 bump for int4 on our 4090 fleet and I want to rule out regresses before the rollout.

akshay: which workload / sequence length? and do you have the exact commit/worker image?

maria: seq=512, batch=1 typical PLG path. Nightly job: ref commit 8f3b2a3 (runtime scheduler change). Worker image: rwinf/serve:2026-03-10-rc.

jasper: I can run the microbench and a small eval set. Command I usually use:```bash
python tools/qbench.py --model model-x --profiles int4,int8,fp8 --seq 512 --batch 1 --runs 20 --warmup 5 --out /tmp/qbench_modelx.csv
```

maria: thanks — also include KV-cache warmup (generate 64 tokens) and a no-cache cold run to compare tail behavior.

bench-bot: queued job 4921 for jasper on pool gpu-4090-a. ETA ~12m. Will post artifacts when done. :gear:

sofia: for quality we should run the core promptset (eval/core100) + the dialogue cases that hit long-context. Add eval flags: `--eval-set eval/core100 --eval-opts "--max_toks 2048"`

jasper: noted. running with your eval flags. also enabling perf traces: `--trace nvtx` so we can see kernel hotspots.

(12m later)

bench-bot: job 4921 finished. summary attached inline:
- int4: P50 8.3ms, P95 29.1ms, mean 10.2ms
- int8: P50 7.9ms, P95 25.4ms, mean 9.6ms
- fp8: P50 8.0ms, P95 24.9ms, mean 9.5ms
Quality diffs vs float32 (core100):
- int4: perplexity +0.32, rouge-L -0.6
- int8: perplexity +0.08, rouge-L -0.1
- fp8: perplexity +0.05, rouge-L +0.0
Full CSV: s3://rwinf-artifacts/qbench/4921/qbench_modelx.csv

maria: those numbers match the nightly bump for int4 P95. Any kernel spikes in the nvtx trace?

jasper: nvtx shows occasional larger matmul kernels at step boundaries when KV-cache fill happens. Looks like batching/granularity change in the new scheduler causes more frequent kernel launches for int4 kernels.

akshay: hmm. scheduler change probably split some fused ops? can you paste the trace snippet?

jasper: snippet:```
[ 0.002s ] matmul_int4_sgemm_kern (launch 1) 0.9ms
[ 0.015s ] matmul_int4_sgemm_kern (launch 2) 1.2ms
[ 0.120s ] matmul_int4_sgemm_kern (launch 3) 6.8ms <-- tail
```

sofia: why bigger at launch 3? maybe backend compaction / cache miss leading to slower path in that moment. Could be memory allocator fragmentation or a fallback to a non-optimized kernel.

akshay: I'll repro locally with the scheduler patch toggled. If it's scheduler-caused, easy to gate with a rollout flag.

maria: also note the int4 quality delta is still small but visible on a few prompt families. Can we run a smaller focused eval for edge prompts that fail? I'll open a PR with the prompt list.

maria: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2748 — contains failing prompts + reproducer harness (small beam eval).

jasper: nice. I can attach trace + perf csv to the PR. akshay do you want me to bisect the scheduler change range?

akshay: yes pls, bisect the scheduler commit window and run qbench short-run (runs=5) for int4 P95. I'll set a script to auto-bisect after getting initial local repro.

ci-bot: NOTE: added a short perf CI job for PR 2748 that runs with int4/int8/fp8 profiles on a single 4090. Results will be posted as a comment.

sofia: if we confirm kernel fallback is the issue, we should add an optimization ticket to avoid the fallback in the hot path for int4 and maybe tweak allocator thresholds.

maria: agreed. For next steps: 1) akshay bisects scheduler, 2) jasper attaches traces + CSV to PR, 3) sofia opens opt ticket if kernel fallback confirmed. Anyone volunteer to watch CI job and flag if P95 > 28ms for int4?

jasper: I'll watch CI and post a summary.

maria: thanks all — ping here with results. :pray:
